Kehel

Overview

Kehel is a disgraced necromancer living in the Last Shelter. Bitter about the Guild’s intrigues, he interprets generosity and honour as disguises for greed and revenge. He asks Zak to destroy a harpy from his experiments and directs the search for At-Zako toward Joon scholars and the rival necromancer Kholai. He recognises that the teleport amulet’s destination can only be read by a Great Magician. [1, 2, 3, 4]

The Blacksmith’s revenge and Kehel’s experiment

The Shelter’s inhabitants can ask for help with their own grievances alongside the search for At-Zako. Brother Blacksmith wants the slavedriver brothers Lash-Aga and Whip-Aga killed at the plantations. If Zak carries out the request, the workers raise the alarm instead of helping him. The smith explains that imperial law threatens them with death if they fail to report a stranger, then promises to repay the revenge. Kehel offers a separate commission: destroy a harpy he once experimented on, so rivals cannot claim his work. After its death, he admits that fear of Zak’s strength is what makes him honour the promised reward. Their requests expose different consequences of life under the empire: coerced obedience among the workers, personal revenge among its fugitives, and rivalry among its scholars. [5, 6, 2, 7, 8, 9]

Kholai and the dead scientist

Kehel directs Zak to Kholai, whom Taivo displaced from the imperial laboratory. Kholai wants disgrace for his rival rather than a simple assassination. Zak steals a dead scientist’s head from the laboratory; its disappearance will embarrass Taivo, and Kholai can summon its spirit. The scientist describes a horror pursuing the red-skinned youth. To conceal him, the scholars changed his appearance and sent him away by teleportation. Kholai interprets the broken testimony and tells Zak to search the ruined mansion for the magical object used in the escape. The fragments Zak finds are beyond Kehel’s ability to interpret: only a Great Magician can identify the destination. Kholai can also give Zak an experimental object to test in combat. He is interested in the result even if the trial kills its user, a further sign of the limits of his concern for his visitor. [3, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 4, 15]
